system.name: LoopTailor
system.one_liner: an end-to-end VSync regulator that decouples game rendering from the cloud pipeline and coordinates VSync timing with the client

components.name: MCG-X
components.role: one of three compared mobile cloud gaming architectures; renders inside a Guest VM and forwards frames via a Host with a sub-millisecond Projection step

components.name: Google Android Emulator
components.role: a Guest-VM-based MCG architecture compared alongside MCG-X, forwarding Context/Resource/Drawing APIs to its Host over RPC

components.name: DroidCloud
components.role: a container-based MCG architecture (no guest VM) that maps Context/Resource/Drawing APIs to a separate Rendering Backend

components.name: Game Rendering
components.role: grouping box covering the VM-based rendering stage shared by MCG-X and Google Android Emulator

components.name: Guest VM
components.role: virtualized guest environment in which the game renders; used by both MCG-X and Google Android Emulator

components.name: Container
components.role: lightweight OS-level container DroidCloud uses instead of a guest VM

components.name: Host
components.role: host-side component that composites and forwards guest rendering output; paired with each Guest VM

components.name: Rendering Backend
components.role: host-side rendering component paired with DroidCloud's Container

components.name: Shadow Contexts
components.role: MCG-X's guest-side mechanism tracked before Host-side projection

components.name: Resource Handles
components.role: MCG-X's guest-side resource references passed to the Host

components.name: Context APIs
components.role: graphics context calls forwarded via RPC from the Guest VM/Container to the Host/Rendering Backend, used by Google Android Emulator and DroidCloud

components.name: Resource APIs
components.role: resource-handling calls forwarded via RPC from the Guest VM/Container to the Host/Rendering Backend, used by Google Android Emulator and DroidCloud

components.name: Drawing APIs
components.role: drawing calls forwarded via RPC from the Guest VM/Container to the Host/Rendering Backend, used by Google Android Emulator and DroidCloud

components.name: Projection
components.role: MCG-X's Host-side step projecting the guest's shadow contexts/resource handles into a frame (~0.0 ms)

components.name: Layer Composition
components.role: shared downstream pipeline stage that composites the rendered frame

components.name: Virtual Display
components.role: shared downstream pipeline stage presenting the composited frame to a virtual display

components.name: Frame Encoding
components.role: shared downstream pipeline stage encoding the frame for network transmission

components.name: Client
components.role: end device receiving the encoded frame, triggering VSync5

components.name: Input Injection
components.role: entry point where player input is injected for MCG-X/Google Android Emulator, triggering VSync1

components.name: Input Mapping
components.role: DroidCloud's entry point mapping player input into its Container, triggering VSync1

summary: This paper introduces LoopTailor, an end-to-end VSync regulator that streamlines mobile cloud gaming's interactive loop. Rather than showing LoopTailor itself, Figure 19 compares three baseline mobile cloud gaming (MCG) architectures side by side: MCG-X and the Google Android Emulator both inject input into a Guest VM (via Shadow Contexts/Resource Handles or Context/Resource/Drawing APIs over RPC) that a paired Host composites, while DroidCloud instead maps input into a lightweight Container served by a separate Rendering Backend. All three converge on a shared downstream pipeline of Layer Composition, Virtual Display, and Frame Encoding before reaching the Client. Latency numbers labeled on the arrows (roughly 0.3-2.5 ms per stage) quantify each architecture's overhead, and VSync1 through VSync5 mark the timing events each design must synchronize across the guest/host or container/backend boundary.

notes: layout-proposal: stacked-pipeline-comparison — three architecture variants (MCG-X, Google Android Emulator, DroidCloud) are stacked as rows, each a short input-to-rendering pipeline annotated with per-stage latency, converging into one shared downstream pipeline (Layer Composition to Client). No body paragraph mentions this figure, so components and roles are read from the caption and figure only; note the figure itself labels this system 'MCG-X' although the paper's running text elsewhere calls it 'X-MCG'.
